marta: Heads-up — after last night's attn-layout change + quant-profile flip, we're seeing a significant drop in context-prefix cache hit-rate for a subset of customer traffic. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/prefix-cache/alerts :eyes:
kevin: which change exactly? commit hash, quant profile name?
marta: commit 3b9f7c4 (attn layout rewrite -> fused_matmul + fused_attn_v2). quant profile rolled: q4_optim_v2 at 02:10 UTC. kernel variant rotated in runtime.
jia: numbers? is this global or a narrow route?
marta: narrow to chat-short (lead tokens 1-4) but affects ~18% of overall requests for that route. baseline hit-rate ~97.8% pre-rollout; post-rollout steady ~64.1%. p95 latency for small prompts up ~18ms. Repro logs attached: ```[2026-03-17T02:13:14Z] route=chat-short model=rwkv-v1 kernel=fused_attn_v2 kv_key=sha1:af3b... hit=false```
marta: repro command: `./infra/bench -route chat-short -model rwkv-v1 -traffic 1000 --seed 42 --track-prefix-hits`
kevin: interesting — did we change any canonicalization or padding order in the fused kernel?
marta: fused_attn_v2 changes tensor layout (N, S, D) -> (S, N, D) for matmul path and pads differently for tail blocks. There was also a tiny tokenizer tweak earlier today.
sam: iirc tokenizer PR 5a2d altered NBSP handling when normalizing leading whitespace. could be related. :thinking_face: 
jia: KV keying: runtime key = hash(build_id + model_ver + raw_prefix_bytes + tokenizer_norm). If tokenizer_norm changes, keys will differ even for semantically identical prefixes.
kevin: so possible causes: (1) tokenizer normalization diff -> different bytes, (2) kernel padding changes producing different bytes passed into keyer (if we key on raw buffer), (3) quant rounding leading to different serialized cache keys in some code path.
marta: quick local experiment: repro with `--no-token-normalize` (force old behavior) -> local hit-rate back to 96.9%. That pretty strongly implicates normalization.
sam: nice — can we run a diff of normalized bytes for failing vs passing examples?
marta: did that: examples show NBSP (0xC2 0xA0) present in the original client texts; old normalizer converted NBSP -> space, new normalizer left NBSP in some code paths. So identical visible text -> different normalized bytes -> cache miss.
jia: mitigation options: 1) runtime canonicalization patch (strip/normalize NBSP + collapse whitespace) before hashing keys; 2) pin kernel variant for warmup routes to fused_attn_v1 until we fix tokenizer; 3) backfill cache by rekeyer for affected build_id/model combinations.
kevin: plan: apply quick canonicalization in runtime (low-risk), run canary for 1 hour. If that recovers hit-rate -> merge full fix. If not, rollback kernel variant for high-impact customers.
infra-bot: rollback schedule: none currently. created ticket RW-1261 investigating prefix-cache regression.
marta: I'll open PR with canonicalization + unit tests and add an e2e that asserts identical normalized-bytes between old and new tokenizers for NBSP cases. Also adding a debug flag to log normalized hex for failed prefix hits.
kevin: can you also capture a small histogram for affected route? we need pre/post numbers in the ticket.
marta: pasted quick numbers inline: pre-rollout (2026-03-16 23:00): hit 97.8%, miss 2.2%. post-rollout (2026-03-17 03:00): hit 64.1%, miss 35.9%. warmup median time: pre 1.9s -> post 5.3s.
sam: ouch. thanks for the quick triage.
jia: i'll start a canary with the canonicalization patch on 5% of traffic and report back by 11:30 PT.
marta: if canary looks good, we'll promote and then run a rekey job to pre-populate caches for the rest. If canary fails, rollback kernel variant for the route and iterate.
kevin: sounds good. assign owners in RW-1261 and mark customer impact P1.
sam: :thumbsup:
kevin: one more note — add a metric that breaks prefix-hits by tokenizer-normalization-version so we can catch this earlier next time.
marta: on it. I'll add to the rollout checklist that any tokenizer changes must include a no-op canonicalization test against live prefix keys.
